newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks pop up at open aided by golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks pop up at open aided by golds.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks inched to new highs at Wednesday's open, aided by stronger golds. * Most of 14 sub-indexes gained ground. *Turnover of 7 million shares valued at C$111 million.
Toronto stocks tacked on more gains at Wednesday's open, lifted by strong bonds, golds and higher quarterly corporate earnings.

"Bonds are on the plus side again," said Peter Chandler, C.M. Oliver & Co Ltd's senior vice-president. "It's more fuel for the market fire." Canada's benchmark 30-year bond jumped C$0.85 to C$122.08, yielding 6.341 percent and helping banks.
Also, "the market is still being largely driven by companies with predictable earnings," Chandler added. More earnings are forecast for today, including Canadian Airlines Corp and Air Canada.
Investors are still putting their money into equities as the rally grows, analysts said. "There's a lot of money still on the sidelines," Chandler said.
Almost all of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors gained ground. The lone decliner was conglomerates. The stronger side was powered by transportation, pipelines, oils and key golds.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners 253 to 160, while 199 traded flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Toronto-Dominion Bank topped actives, rising 0.45 to 43.55 on more than 1.28 million shares.

* Laidlaw Inc LDM.TO rose 0.25 to 21.55. North America's largest school bus and emergency transportation company continued its acquisitive ways with Wednesday's news that it snapped up Dallas-based Emcare Holdings Inc for $400 million cash or $38 a share.
* Integrated energy firm Petro-Canada Inc jumped 0.45 to 24.5 after being upgraded to outperform from neutral by Morgan Stanley.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
